============================== Cable Sizing DC
A1=CABLE SIZING  -  DC string / array cable   (H1Z2Z2-K copper XLPE, 2 loaded conductors)
A2=Colour key:  NAVY bar = sheet title or table header  ·  PALE BLUE bar = section  ·  YELLOW = input you edit (blue text) or value imported from another sheet (green text)  ·  GOLD = grouping input  ·  no fill = calculated  ·  light blue cell in the reference tables = the value in use.  Every formula on this sheet reads only cells on THIS sheet: imported figures come in once, at section 1.

A26=Design I/cable = design current / Parallel N.  Util colour: green <=80%, amber <=100%, red >100%.  GROUPING per IEC 60364-5-52 B.52.18/19 NOTE 3 (and the same principle for MV): a circuit with m parallel conductors per phase counts as m circuits, so Own circuits = circuits routed together x Parallel N. Put any OTHER loaded cables sharing the trench or tray in "Aux circuits". The factor is looked up on the TOTAL. Unloaded cables (earth, fibre, spares) do not count.
A28=5.  VOLTAGE DROP
A29=R is per metre of conductor. A DC circuit is a loop, so total conductor length = route x loop factor (2 = out and return; set 1 if your R already covers both legs).

A22=Design I/cable = design current / Parallel N.  Util colour: green <=80%, amber <=100%, red >100%.  GROUPING per IEC 60364-5-52 B.52.18/19 NOTE 3 (and the same principle for MV): a circuit with m parallel conductors per phase counts as m circuits, so Own circuits = circuits routed together x Parallel N. A24=5.  VOLTAGE DROP
A25=dV = root3 x I x (R cos(theta) + X sin(theta)) x L.  Power loss = 3 x I^2 x R x L.  Pick a cable from the library or edit R and X directly.

A217=EXTRAPOLATED - NOT IEC DATA.  The purple 500 and 630 mm2 rows are linearly extrapolated from the 300 and 400 mm2 tabulated ratings, with a safety reduction applied. IEC 60502-2 Table B.3 is tabulated only to 400 mm2. Real ratings flatten off above 400 mm2 as skin and proximity effects grow, so straight-line extrapolation over-predicts and the reduction is there to offset that - it is a placeholder, not a calculated value. Obtain manufacturer ratings (Nexans, Prysmian, NKT publish BS6622 33 kV aluminium data computed to IEC 60287) and type them over these cells before issuing any design.
